name: Sergei Parfenov
description: Sergei Parfenov, CTO at Aliwio and Symptomato. Early Yandex Praktikum team member building AI products, learning infrastructure and automated project assessment.
summary: Engineering, product and the work in between.
intro: Over the past decade, my work has grown from software engineering into building AI products, launching a startup and leading technical teams.
homeStory: I was part of the early team behind Yandex Praktikum. At TripleTen, I built AI assessment, search and tutoring systems, and helped launch the QA programme in the US. One of those assessment systems made grading 14 times faster.
I also co-founded IAWY, an AI tutor that reviews student projects and supports learners. We launched it in two bootcamps in Latin America. The project was featured in Tech.eu.
homeCurrent: Today I’m CTO at Aliwio and Symptomato, working on veterinary software and a healthcare service that combines AI with human expertise.
blogIntro: I share experiments, technical deep dives and what I learn building AI systems. Nearly 10k subscribers follow my writing.
about: I joined Yandex Praktikum as the 11th person on the team and helped build the product from its earliest stages. I worked across multiple components, designed the test architecture for its coding trainer, used by 7,000–10,000 students a day, and developed an ML model to assess student project submissions. This was before ChatGPT.

I also helped launch the QA Engineering programme in the US. At TripleTen, my work connected AI, backend engineering and the learning experience, including personalisation and the Mastery Depth Tracker.
I spent about a year developing IAWY, a startup for automated review of student project work. We launched the product in two bootcamps in Latin America.

Today I’m CTO at two projects: Aliwio, a veterinary CRM, and Symptomato, a service combining AI intake with human health specialists. I’m based in Barcelona and work across product decisions, architecture and implementation.

currentRoles.description: Building a veterinary CRM for independent clinics — from the technical architecture to the product itself.
Leading technology for a service where AI gathers context before a human health specialist joins the conversation.

writing: I write about AI engineering: experiments, systems that break, and what the measurements actually tell us. My writing reaches nearly 10k subscribers.

collaboration.title: We could work together.
collaboration.description: An early product to build, an AI hypothesis to test, or a system that needs to work for thousands of people. I bring the engineering and product decisions together.
collaboration.approach: I can turn an idea into a testable first version, work through the architecture and implementation, and help the team decide what to build next. I explain the technical trade-offs in terms of the product and the people using it.
collaboration.invitation: Tell me what you’re building, where you’re stuck and what a useful result would look like.

capabilities.name: An AI idea worth testing
capabilities.description: Turn an uncertain idea into a focused experiment. Build a working prototype, test the hypothesis and use what we learn to decide what deserves a full product — before committing to a big build.

capabilities.name: Building an early product
capabilities.description: Work across the first version, architecture, backend and interface. Make decisions with the team about what to build now, what to leave out and how to take the product into real use.

capabilities.name: Agents you can evaluate
capabilities.description: Find out why an agent fails, not just whether its answer looks plausible. Build checks around tool use, memory, retrieval and recovery, with traces you can inspect and tests you can repeat.

capabilities.name: Smaller models, measured trade-offs
capabilities.description: Explore distillation and fine-tuning for a narrow task. Compare the smaller model with a baseline on quality, speed and memory before deciding whether the trade is worth it.

capabilities.name: Learning platforms & automated assessment
capabilities.description: Design test architecture for coding trainers, ML assessment of project submissions, and feedback that helps students make progress. Connect those systems to the curriculum, learner confidence and retention.

projects.name: Screenshot model distillation
projects.description: A 7B-to-2B vision-model experiment, with a reproducible training and evaluation pipeline. A small proof of concept, including where the metrics misled me.

projects.name: Agent memory & provenance

experience.description: I’m responsible for the technical architecture and product engineering of a CRM for independent veterinary clinics.
I lead technology at Symptomato. The service uses an AI assistant to gather context, then brings a human health specialist into the conversation.
I built AI assessment, retrieval and tutoring systems, working from architecture through production releases.
highlights: Designed and implemented a plan and execute assessment system. Reduced grading latency from 8.4 seconds to 0.6 seconds, a 14× speedup, and replaced 140 legacy text-area quizzes.
Built a Kafka based CMS vectorization pipeline processing 100,000 items a day. Delivered semantic search end to end, increasing search engagement by 9% and reducing time to content by 18%.
Built automatic practice generation that cut task authoring from 2.5 hours to 18 minutes. Shipped an internal VS Code plugin that reduced average support time per student issue by 27%.

Worked on Voice Mode for AI Tutor (Dot), connecting WebRTC, speech recognition, an LLM and speech synthesis. Helped bring it to a stable release with 97.8% successful sessions and a 1.3 second median first response.

I helped shape learning personalisation and built features that improved student retention. On the Mastery Depth Tracker, I connected product and engineering to measure learners’ confidence and identify where they needed more practice. I also helped launch the QA Engineering programme in the US.

experience.description: I co-founded and developed IAWY, a startup for automated review of student project submissions. I defined the product vision and roadmap for an AI tutor that integrated into existing learning platforms. We successfully launched it in two bootcamps in Latin America.
Designed a product listing enrichment pipeline: normalizing input data, extracting attributes, generating structured features and writing natural language descriptions.
I was the 11th person to join the team and one of the people who built the product from its earliest stages, contributing across multiple components.
